home.h1: I collect cards, complete binders, and give them away.
home.p1: I pick up Pokémon cards from card shops around Europe and the United States, organise them into binders, and give a binder away when it is complete. The binders go to children: a hospital ward, a shelter, an after-school club. I write down each one that leaves.
home.p2: This site is the record. The counts start at zero and move only when a shipment is real.
home.setBody: A set binder holds every card from one set. Paldean Fates is the idea in miniature: the whole set, with nothing left out on purpose.
home.genBody: A generation binder holds one card of every species from that generation, from any set. Generation 1 is the original 151. Generations 1 through 9 are 1,025 species.
home.bulkBody: A Magikarp from a bulk box is as welcome as a holo. I am gathering different cards, and one of each Pokémon. I am not building a collection to sell, and this site does not say what a card would sell for.
home.deltaBody: I am getting a binder ready before the card list exists. The page keeps only what Pokémon has published, and the checklist stays empty until the numbers are real.
home.progressZero: Nothing has been logged yet. Every figure here is zero until I record a real shipment.
home.progressLive: These figures come from shipments I have logged.
home.progressError: The count did not load. I would rather show this note than invent a number.
home.thanksEmpty: No shop from these countries has sent cards yet. Names will show up here after the first parcel.
home.shopsP1: Spare cards and bulk you do not need are what I am looking for. Write to me at magnus@linksforcards.com and tell me what you can send.
home.shopsP2: In return I trade a bit of SEO help for Pokémon cards — trading up, quietly, one shipment at a time.
home.shopsP3: Shops that send cards are thanked by name, with an ordinary link to the shop.
home.faq1a: I'm Magnus Schmidt. I collect Pokémon cards, complete binders, and give a binder away when it is full. This page is my public record.
home.faq2q: Do you show what a card is worth?
home.faq2a: No. The public pages show counts and names. They never show a pound or euro value.
home.faq3q: Is this an official Pokémon site?
home.faq3a: No. LinksForCards is my unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Creatures, Game Freak, or The Pokémon Company.
home.faq4a: This page lists shops in the United Kingdom and Ireland. The US English page lists shops in the United States.
home.cupRules: One point for each card a shop sends, and bulk counts. A binder in the parcel adds 1,000 points. The country is the shop's country.
home.cupEmpty: Which country will be first on the board?
home.cupError: The board did not load. I would rather show this note than invent a score.

privacy.p1: I run this site myself. I am Magnus Schmidt, and you can reach me at magnus@linksforcards.com.
privacy.p2: The public pages do not ask you to sign in. I do not use advertising or analytics cookies. Choosing a language is a link, and it does not set a cookie.
privacy.p3: If you email me, I keep that correspondence so I can reply, and so I can remember what was said about a shipment. You can ask me to correct or delete what you sent.
privacy.p4: The private admin area sets one session cookie after I sign in. That cookie keeps the session. It is not set for people reading the public pages.
privacy.p5: The host that serves the site may keep technical logs, including IP addresses, for a short time as part of running it. Shipments I log, and the private price estimates, sit in a database I configure. Public pages show counts, thanks, notes, and handovers. They do not show prices.
privacy.p6: I do not sell personal information. If this text changes, I will update it here. The postal address is on the imprint.

printChecklist.indexDescription: Free checklists for every set, themed binder, and generation. Each line has a number, a name, and a rarity, with a box to tick on paper.
printChecklist.indexIntro: I print a list when I sort cards into a binder. A set list and a themed list, such as every Pikachu, show the collector number, the card name, and the rarity. A generation list, such as Generation 1 · Kanto, is one line per Pokémon, and any printing fills that line. Each line has an empty box. I tick the box when the card is in the pocket. The lists are free to print or save as a PDF. Card names and set names stay in English, the way they are printed on the card.
printChecklist.indexPaper: The print view follows the paper size you choose in the browser, so the same list suits A4 and US Letter. Each PDF is one of those sizes.
